subject: Hosted API pricing — Avocet usage slabs & parity request
messages:
From: Ella Thompson <ella@avocethealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@avocethealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing parity request for upcoming pilot

Hi Jasmine,

Quick intro — I run procurement at Avocet Health. We’re kicking off a clinical documentation pilot and evaluating hosted LLM providers. Based on usage projections (roughly 1.2B tokens/month at steady state across inference and embedding calls) the economics are the key driver for our vendor selection.

We’ve been quoted $0.0008/token equivalent from one of your competitors for their high-volume committed tier. Before we go deeper, can Redwood match that per-token rate for equivalent model capability and SLA?

If matching is possible, we’ll prioritize a short pilot (30–45 days) with a view to a 12‑month commit. Please include any constraints (streaming, embedding vs generation splits, or required reserved capacity).

Thanks —
Ella
Ella Thompson
Procurement, Avocet Health
ella@avocethealth.com


From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Thompson <ella@avocethealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing parity request for upcoming pilot

Hi Ella — thanks for the note and the clear volume guidance.

Short answer: we want to be competitive, but there are a couple of product/contract nuances to line up before we can confirm a hard $/token parity. Key points to confirm from your side: expected split between chat/generation vs embedding calls, % of streaming usage (if any), and whether you need SOC2 + audit log export as part of the pilot.

Tentative offer we can start from and iterate on: a usage slab structure with a 6–12 month committed minimum and a performance SLA for hosted API. For a 12‑month commit at the volumes you quoted we could potentially approach ~$0.00085–$0.00090/token for the top slab, subject to model selection and whether you require reserved capacity.

I’ve looped in Rafael to drop a proposed slab table and Lauren who’s supporting the account. If Avocet can share a target contract timeline, that will help us accelerate internal approvals.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai

On 2026-10-04 at 09:12, Ella Thompson wrote:
> Quick intro — I run procurement at Avocet Health. We’re kicking off a clinical documentation pilot...

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Thompson <ella@avocethealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing parity request for upcoming pilot — proposed slab rates and notes

Ella / Jasmine — following up with a concrete starting point. Please see the proposed slab pricing below (per-token equivalent, USD):

- Slab A: 0–200M tokens/month: $0.00120
- Slab B: 200M–1B tokens/month: $0.00095
- Slab C: >1B tokens/month: $0.00085

Notes and assumptions:
- These numbers assume standard hosted API with Redwood model variants (non-dedicated). If you require reserved capacity / dedicated GPUs for strict latency SLOs, add-on fees apply (we can include a committed reserved capacity discount).
- Streaming token handling (real-time token emission) is priced the same per token but can affect latency tail guarantees; if >=30% streaming we’ll need an operational review.
- Embeddings vs generation: embeddings counted as 0.6x token-equivalent for billing in this proposal (we can change if Avocet prefers 1:1).
- 12‑month term preferred for the Slab C floor; 6‑month pilot pricing would sit ~10–15% higher.

Attached: proposed_ratecard.csv (breakout by model family and example monthly cost at forecasted usage).

We’ve included a modest volume-based incentive: if you exceed 1.5B tokens/month for two consecutive months, we can add a one-time credit equal to 2% of that month’s bill toward the following month.

If Avocet needs parity down to $0.00080/token for Slab C, we’ll need a binding 12‑month commit, a minimal annual CPI escalation (3%), and a mutual SLA (99.9% regional uptime) plus a PS engagement for migration.

Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing parity request for upcoming pilot — approval constraints

Looping in quick commercial constraints from RevOps:

- Discount floor for hosted API is $0.00083/token for sustained >1B commits — anything lower requires head of revenue approval.
- We can route the request for $0.00080/token to leadership, but it will require: (a) signed 12‑month MRR commit (b) a minimum irrevocable PO and (c) legal signoff on indemnities.
- As a concession for procurement friction, we can offer free audit log export for the pilot (one-time export + 30 days retention in the customer-owned bucket).

If Avocet confirms 1.2B/month baseline and a 12‑month contract, I’m comfortable greenlighting a final slab at $0.00083/token for Slab C with legal/finance review.

Vivek
Director, Revenue Operations
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Mike Carter <mike.carter@avocethealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ella Thompson <ella@avocethealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@avocethealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — Avocet usage slabs & parity request

Jasmine / Rafael — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clarity. We appreciate the slab table and the flexibility.

Avocet can agree in principle to a 12‑month committed arrangement targeting 1.2B tokens/month, subject to the following:
1) Redwood confirms Slab C floor at $0.00083/token for volumes >1B with an explicit line in the order form;
2) We get audit log export for the pilot and 30 days retention as proposed;
3) Legal needs a redline on your standard MSA (we’ll mark up a few liability items) — we need DocuSign start this week to hit our procurement cutover by 10/31.

We attach a one-page PO stub to accelerate the process (avocet_po_stub.pdf). Please send a redline / DocuSign link and I’ll have procurement queue it up.

-Mike
Mike Carter
Director, Clinical Innovation
Avocet Health
